item.text: [{"taxonId":56437,"summary":"A liverwort species with a cosmopolitan distribution, greasewort grows in damp places ranging from open ground to partial shade. Its thick, fleshy, ribbon-like body is dark green when wet and nearly black when dry; it readily colonizes bare ground but is easily displaced by competing plants.","humanEdibility":"unknown","edibilityNote":null,"evidence":{"summary":["s1:p1","s1:p2","s1:p3"],"humanEdibility":[]}},{"taxonId":56451,"summary":"A liverwort species, Rock Veilwort favors damp hollows and woodlands, particularly on limestone-rich surfaces. It sometimes grows on tree bark, including ash in humid wooded valleys, but is threatened by the loss of cool, moist habitats.","humanEdibility":"unknown","edibilityNote":null,"evidence":{"summary":["s1:p2","s1:p3","s1:p4"],"humanEdibility":[]}},{"taxonId":56459,"summary":"A family of liverworts whose included genera have occupied separate regions: Pellia in the temperate Northern Hemisphere and Noteroclada in the Southern Hemisphere, though the latter is now placed in another family. Noteroclada looks leafy, while Pellia has a flatter, less leafy form; the uncommon Androcryphia resembles leafy liverworts of another order.","humanEdibility":"unknown","edibilityNote":null,"evidence":{"summary":["s1:p1"],"humanEdibility":[]}},{"taxonId":56465,"summary":"A liverwort species recorded in Europe, Asia and both North and South America, Comb Liverwort inhabits damp ground, springs, bogs and wet rocks. Its creeping or rising body branches regularly into a dense, comb-like form and ranges from green to brown, becoming black when dry.","humanEdibility":"unknown","edibilityNote":null,"evidence":{"summary":["s1:p2","s1:p3","s1:p4"],"humanEdibility":[]}},{"taxonId":56477,"summary":"A genus of liverworts in the family Lepidoziaceae, Bazzania had 258 accepted species as of November 2024.","humanEdibility":"unknown","edibilityNote":null,"evidence":{"summary":["s1:p1","s1:p2"],"humanEdibility":[]}},{"taxonId":56484,"summary":"A genus of liverworts with a cosmopolitan distribution, Calypogeia belongs to the family Calypogeiaceae.","humanEdibility":"unknown","edibilityNote":null,"evidence":{"summary":["s1:p1","s1:p2"],"humanEdibility":[]}},{"taxonId":56485,"summary":"A liverwort species native to Europe, Africa, Asia and North America, Common Pouchwort forms pale-green patches on loamy soil in woodland ravines and banks. Its loosely overlapping, egg-shaped leaves usually have bent, two-toothed tips; it rarely produces spores but often forms small asexual reproductive bodies.","humanEdibility":"unknown","edibilityNote":null,"evidence":{"summary":["s1:p2","s1:p3","s1:p4"],"humanEdibility":[]}},{"taxonId":56497,"summary":"A genus of liverworts, Cephaloziella includes C. varians, the only liverwort occurring in continental Antarctica.","humanEdibility":"unknown","edibilityNote":null,"evidence":{"summary":["s1:p1"],"humanEdibility":[]}},{"taxonId":56503,"summary":"A low-growing liverwort found across Europe to Iceland and western Russia, and in parts of Asia, North Africa and North America, Pale Liverwort occupies moist or wet ground rich in lime. It forms pale, translucent yellow-green to brown-green patches and has lower leaves deeply split into two long, narrow lobes.","humanEdibility":"unknown","edibilityNote":null,"evidence":{"summary":["s1:p2","s1:p3"],"humanEdibility":[]}},{"taxonId":56519,"summary":"A genus of liverworts and the sole genus in the family Frullaniaceae, Frullania includes living species and four named extinct species documented from Cenomanian Burmese amber in Myanmar.","humanEdibility":"unknown","edibilityNote":null,"evidence":{"summary":["s1:p1","s1:p27"],"humanEdibility":[]}}]
